mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last three weeks with an accelerating weekly decline (-2.5, -9.7, -14.9 points). This momentum reflects entrenched reduced foot traffic that will persist, producing a lower 28-day mean for RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the past 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:weekly decline accelerated from -2.5 to -9.7 to -14.9 points over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rebounds within two weeks such that the next-28-day mean exceeds the last-28-day mean, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above +17 percent for two consecutive weeks signals an active or tightening stay-at-home directive. Once this threshold is crossed, non-essential retail trips are further suppressed, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mean exceeds +17 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 13.7 to 18.7 over the four-week window, crossing +17 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +17 for two or more weeks, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate compounding reductions in both commuting and work-based trip chains that normally feed adjacent retail visits. Their joint decline removes a larger share of incidental retail footfall than either series alone would predict, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT (-50.4 to -59.6) and WORKPLACES (-36.6 to -46.1) declined in parallel over the four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises or stays flat despite continued joint decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The co-movement of falling WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside rising RESIDENTIAL is characteristic of a tightening-restrictions regime where authorities are actively discouraging mobility. Under this regime, retail trip suppression intensifies and RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series moved consistently (WORKPLACES and TRANSIT down, RESIDENTIAL up) across all four weeks
failure_condition: If this co-movement pattern persists but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than the last-28-day mean, the regime-conditional mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: After three consecutive weeks of RETAIL_REC declines exceeding 10 points, a saturation effect emerges: essential retail and pharmacy needs create a behavioral floor that limits further contraction, producing a short-term rebound in RETAIL_REC within the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly decline exceeds 10 points for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:weekly decline reached -14.9 points in the most recent week, the largest of the four-week window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's weekly mean continues to decline for the next week rather than rebounding, the saturation/mean-reversion mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained within a narrow band (-14.6 to -17.0) across all four weeks, indicating a stable floor of essential-trip behavior that anchors overall out-of-home activity. This stability signals that further collapse in RETAIL_REC is unlikely, supporting a modest recovery over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within a 3-point band for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only between -14.6 and -17.0 over the four-week window
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean continues to fall relative to the last 28 days, the stabilizing-floor mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-to-week swings in PARKS (-3.6, -12.0, -1.6, -7.7) suggest volatile weather conditions. When outdoor park use is seasonally suppressed, some discretionary trips shift toward enclosed retail and recreation venues, producing a modest upward pressure on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS shows non-monotonic swings of over 8 points between consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS volatility persists without any corresponding uptick in RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES declines by more than 5 points week-on-week at the same time TRANSIT falls below -55, the combination indicates an escalating formal mobility restriction that specifically targets commuting and shared transit, amplifying suppression of retail trips beyond what either series alone would cause, and lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT is below -55
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 4.0 points and TRANSIT reached -59.6 in the most recent week, approaching the joint threshold
failure_condition: If the joint threshold is met but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not fall relative to the last 28 days, the interaction-threshold mechanism is rejected.
